title: Satellite Trail Camera for Hog Traps With No Cell Signal
reader_sentence: If your trap is out where your phone has no signal, a cellular camera can't reach you either, so use a camera that runs on Starlink, like the Starlink version of the HogEye Mini Camera, and you can still watch the trap live and close it from home.

evidence.signal: satellite trail camera 720/mo (1,000 Aug-Nov), starlink camera 320, trail cam that sends pics to phone without wifi 260

key_points: Without cell signal at the trap, a cellular camera can't send you video or take a close command.
The Starlink version of the HogEye Mini Camera is $2,999. It is the same camera and the same HogEye app, but it connects over Wi-Fi through a Starlink Mini receiver instead of a cell connection.
It works almost anywhere the receiver can see open sky.
Data and connectivity are $100 a month through Wildlife Dominion. There is no separate Starlink account or service to buy.
The kit includes the Starlink Mini receiver and a freestanding steel tripod stand: the receiver sits on top and the camera mounts on the side, so you don't need a T-post.
The kit includes a 12V 100Ah lithium battery and a 300W foldable solar panel sized to run both the camera and the receiver.
The kit includes the gate cable and latch adapter that connect the camera to the trap's gate.
The HogEye Mini Camera streams live video to the HogEye app, day or night, with digital pan, tilt, and zoom.
You watch the hogs inside and outside the trap in the app, and when the whole sounder is inside you send the close command from your phone and the gate closes.
Closing on part of a sounder teaches the hogs that got away to avoid the trap.
Several people can watch the same trap; the app allows unlimited users at no extra fee.
